cards.title: Run an Accidental Diminisher self-assessment to find where you cap your team's output
cards.summary: How to use the 10-scenario Accidental Diminisher quiz as a diagnostic for leaders whose management habits may be capping their team's contribution.
cards.use_when: You are an ecommerce owner, head of ecommerce or team lead who suspects your team defers to you constantly — you personally approve every product launch, ad angle or promotion — and you want a structured starting point for diagnosing why.
steps: Recognize the research finding: few Diminishers realize the restrictive impact they have on others. Most moved into management because they were praised for personal intellectual merit and assumed the boss's job was to have the best ideas; others once thought like Multipliers but went native after working among Diminishers. Accidental or not, the impact on your team is the same — the source claims you may be getting only half of the team's true brainpower.

Take the Accidental Diminisher Quiz at www.multipliersbook.com: 10 common management scenarios describing your own approach. It produces an instant 'A.D. Score' (lower is better) plus a report with suggestions for adjusting your leadership practices. Verify the current assessment location and format, since the source references a specific website.

Use your score as a hypothesis, not a verdict. Map the scenarios where you scored worst onto actual ecommerce workflows — category planning, PDP copy, creative briefs, pricing tests, inventory calls — and identify which decisions you currently make alone that the team could make or co-own.
Reflect on the specific behavior behind each weak scenario rather than on your identity as a leader: the quiz measures management patterns, and the source frames these as changeable.

Note the optional next step: for a fuller picture, the source points to a 360-degree assessment or a measure of how much intelligence you or your team accesses from people around you, offered via The Wiseman Group (www.TheWisemanGroup.com, info@TheWisemanGroup.com).
caveats: The quiz is a self-report instrument, so it reflects how you see yourself, not how your team experiences you; a 360-degree assessment is the source's suggested alternative for that reason.
The claim that you may be getting only half your team's brainpower is the source's framing, not a measured benchmark to plan headcount or output against.
Website links, quiz format and scoring may have changed — verify before relying on them.

cards.title: Choose where to apply Multiplier leadership first for the greatest impact
cards.summary: A prioritization step for picking the one domain (business, community or family) where adopting Multiplier practices would matter most before rolling it out.
cards.use_when: You want to roll out a more delegating, idea-generating leadership style in your ecommerce operation but can't change everything at once — e.g. you lead merchandising, marketing and ops and need to decide which function gets the new approach first.
steps: Start from the source's question: across the spheres you operate in (business, community, family), where could you implement the Multiplier approach with the greatest impact, and why? Answer the 'why' explicitly before acting, so the choice is reasoned rather than default.

Translate that to the store: list your functions (product selection, pricing, creative, retention, fulfillment) and score each on how much your personal involvement currently bottlenecks it and how much untapped capability sits in the team.

Pick the function with the largest gap between current bottleneck and available capability — for example, if every ad angle waits on your approval while a junior marketer has strong customer-language insight, start there.

Apply the approach long enough to observe a change in what the team proposes and decides before expanding it to the next function; the source treats this as a deliberate starting point, not a one-time conversion.

If you want a structured rollout rather than an ad hoc one, the source offers a full Multipliers Facilitator Guide at www.multipliersbook.com for bringing Multiplier leadership into workplace conversations. Verify it is still available.
caveats: This is a prioritization prompt from the source, not a tested sequencing method with measured outcomes — treat the choice as a working hypothesis.
Impact is judged qualitatively here; do not attach invented metrics or expect a specific productivity gain.
The facilitator guide's availability and contents may change.
